Header: 2026-11-05 16:00 UTC | Duration: 48m | Attendees: Olivia Chen (Redwood AE), Marcus Li (Redwood SE), Rosa Martinez (CTO, Magellan Ops), Daniel Kim (Head of ML), Evan Brooks (SRE), Priya Shah (Product)

Summary (auto): quick intro, workload sizing, key success criteria = latency < 200ms tail for chat, embedding cost < $0.01 per 1k queries, validate caching reduces token usage by ~30%. Redwood to run benchmarks and provide cost spreadsheet.

[00:00] Olivia: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm olivia from redwood, i'm the ae, with marcus our se. how's everyone doing?
[00:08] Rosa: good, thanks. we've been looking at inference cost and want to scope a pilot to see if Redwood makes sense for production.
[00:15] Marcus: awesome. quick agenda - understand your workloads, define success criteria for the POC, then go through the cost model and knobs like batching and prefix caching, and then timeline. sound good?
[00:25] Daniel: yeah, sounds good. our main goals are accurate embeddings for semantic search, and a chat assistant with sub-200ms p50 latency ideally, p95 as low as possible. cost is a hard constraint - targeting less than $X per month for pilot but we'll give numbers.
[00:40] Olivia: perfect. can you give a quick sketch of traffic? qps, average prompt length, embedding sizes?
[00:49] Daniel: currently embedding traffic is around 8 qps average, peaks at 35 qps during business hours. embeddings are 1536 dims, input tokens usually 50 to 120. Chat traffic is lower qps but higher token per request - roughly 6 qps peak, average 200 tokens per session because we keep a short context.
[01:10] Evan: also note we have strict data residency for logs - all telemetry must stay in EU region for EU customers, and our security team will want KMS integration.
[01:20] Marcus: noted, Redwood private supports VPC and KMS - we can scope that. for the cost model we usually estimate per-token generation and per-embedding unit. rough ballparks: hosted model A per-1k tokens = $0.03 for generation, embeddings roughly $0.0015 per embedding call for that size but it depends on batching and quantization. these are examples not final.
[01:47] Rosa: can you break down how batching and caching change those numbers? that's the main lever for us.
[01:53] Marcus: yeah. batching increases throughput and lowers per-token compute cost but can add latency. Redwood has dynamic batching and configurable max-batch latency windows. for small chat qps we can keep batch windows low (5-10ms) to preserve latency; for embeddings we can tolerate slightly larger batching since it's more throughput-oriented. caching: prefix and KV cache can reduce repeated token generation; for your use case with repeated system prompts and similar user histories, we often see 20-40% token reduction with prefix caching.
[02:25] Daniel: is that 20-40% across the board or only for long-running sessions?
[02:29] Marcus: depends on prompt reuse. for semantic search embeddings there's less reuse, so caching helps less. for chat with recurring templates, it's common. we'll validate with your logs.
[02:36] Olivia: for the POC success criteria - what would you measure? we typically recommend: 1) latency SLOs (p50/p95) for chat 2) cost per 1k tokens and per-embedding 3) quality tolerances (embedding cosine similarity thresholds or recall on a test set) 4) operational constraints (KMS, VPC, audit logs).
[03:00] Rosa: yes those align. for us quality is mandatory: embeddings must achieve within 2% of our current recall on internal eval set. latency p95 must be < 500ms but we want p50 < 200ms if possible. cost target is to reduce current infra spend by 30% or be within X budget.
[03:16] Marcus: we can set benchmarks to measure exactly that. recommended bench: run shadow traffic replay for 1 hour at peak qps, measure p50/p95 and cost per token with different model variants and quantization levels. we'll also try batching configs and prefix cache toggles.
[03:35] Daniel: what's the timeline for getting that set up?
[03:38] Olivia: typical pilot is 4-6 weeks. Week 1: onboarding and infra setup (access, KMS, VPC), week 2: ingest traffic samples and baseline benchmarks, week 3: tuning (batching, caching, quant configs), week 4: validation and final report. if we need additional time for legal/security, that can slip.
[03:58] Evan: security check likely takes a week, but we can run benchmarks in a staging VPC with minimal approvals.
[04:05] Marcus: for cost modeling here is how we derive per-unit numbers: we take model throughput (tokens/s per GPU) * instance cost -> per-token compute cost. then we add infra overhead, networking, and Redwood's platform fee. batching reduces compute per token; quantized variants reduce GPU memory footprint and often increase throughput so lower per-token cost, though quality tradeoffs exist.
[04:30] Daniel: can you give a concrete example for our traffic?
[04:33] Marcus: sure. example scenario (ballpark): chat model medium-1 using fp16 on an A100 equiv: say 250 tokens/s per GPU. at your average chat 6 qps * 200 tokens = 1200 tokens/s peak - so you'd need multiple GPUs or multi-instance routing. but with batching you can achieve higher utilization; e.g., batching can raise effective throughput by ~1.5x, so compute cost per token might drop from $0.03 to $0.02 depending on utilization. embeddings: if embeddings are run on a vector-optimized model at 8 qps avg with batching and on-demand scale, cost per embed might be $0.001 - $0.002 each.
[05:20] Rosa: that chat calc seems like a lot of tokens. do we have options to reduce token counts?
[05:24] Marcus: yes, strategies: prompt compression, summarization of long context, aggressive prefix caching for system prompts, and using a smaller context window by storing embeddings for older turns instead of full raw text. we can help instrument and measure estimated token savings.
[05:40] Daniel: for the pilot can you run a cost sensitivity matrix showing different quant levels (fp16, int8) and batching latencies?
[05:47] Olivia: yes we will. we'll include columns for model variant, quant level, batching window, expected p50/p95 latency, estimated per-token cost, and an expected quality delta where we have data.
[06:00] Evan: about benchmarks - we need to test both hosted Redwood API and a Dedicated/Private config to compare cost and data controls. what's the recommended approach?
[06:10] Marcus: do both in parallel if possible. hosted is fastest to stand up, we can run initial benchmarks there; Dedicated or Private will show you isolation and predictable throughput and may be cheaper at scale depending on your commit. we'll include both in the plan and note any differences in audit logs/KMS integration.
[06:28] Rosa: what about telemetry costs? exporting traces/logs will add cost.
[06:33] Marcus: yep, telemetry and storage are additional. in the cost spreadsheet we separate compute token costs and observability/storage costs.
[06:40] Priya: question: what's the minimal data you need from us to run a realistic replay?
[06:45] Marcus: two weeks of anonymized request logs: timestamps, token counts per request, request type (chat/embedding), and sample prompts. we only need hashed IDs for users, no PII.
[06:56] Daniel: we can provide that. should we also provide current latency histograms and cost per month?
[07:00] Olivia: yes please, current cloud spend numbers and latency p50/p95 help us calibrate.
[07:05] Rosa: timeline wise, legal wants SOC2 report and data processing agreement. can you share Redwood's compliance pack?
[07:12] Olivia: absolutely, i'll send SOC2, ISO and our DPA. note for private deployments we have on-prem guidance and KMS patterns.
[07:20] Daniel: any gotchas about billing surprises? reserved vs consumption?
[07:24] Marcus: reserved/dedicated gives predictable unit economics - you commit and lower per-token compute price. hosted is consumption-based so it's easy to start but can be more expensive at high sustained throughput. we will show both scenarios in the spreadsheet.
[07:36] Rosa: what's a realistic budget line for the pilot? we can commit maybe $20k for 6 weeks but want to understand value.
[07:43] Olivia: with $20k we can run a full 4-6 week pilot including bench runs and some dedicated test capacity. we'll size the pilot to cover peak-hour replay and tuning.
[07:53] Daniel: about quality checks - can Redwood run embedding evals (recall@k) against our reference set?
[07:58] Marcus: yes, we can run embedding evals as part of benchmark and include the metrics in the final report.
[08:05] Priya: do you have any example customers with similar workloads?
[08:08] Olivia: yes we've worked with several search-heavy customers; i'll share anonymized case studies focusing on latency and cost outcomes.
[08:15] Rosa: ok let's talk deliverables again and owners.
[08:18] Olivia: action items: Olivia sends cost model spreadsheet + SOC2 and DPA by Monday 2026-11-09; Marcus will prepare benchmark scripts and staging infra notes by 2026-11-12; customer to share logs and sample prompts by 2026-11-10. proposed bench week of 11/16.
[08:36] Evan: can we run a short smoke test earlier to validate connectivity?
[08:39] Marcus: yes we can do a 1-hour smoke in hosted to validate endpoints with dummy traffic once we have credentials.
[08:45] Daniel: question - can Redwood show token-level cost breakdown in the console for us to reconcile billing?
[08:50] Olivia: yes our console shows token-level cost, per-route breakdown, and per-model breakdown; we'll grant you demo access.
[08:58] Rosa: last thing - if we go dedicated mid-pilot, how disruptive is cutover?
[09:02] Marcus: we support blue-green like rollouts; cutover is a config change and routing update, typically low disruption if planned.
[09:09] Olivia: great, thanks all. we'll follow up with the spreadsheet and schedule the benchmark slot. any final questions?
[09:16] Daniel: none here. thanks.
[09:18] Rosa: thanks everyone.
[09:20] Olivia: thanks, bye.
